stem: How long should a patient who has undergone a Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant (HSCT) wait before receiving live vaccines, assuming no ongoing immunosuppression?
explanation: A two-year window allows the immune system to reconstitute sufficiently to handle the replication of a live attenuated vaccine virus safely.
rationale: This interval is exactly two years post-transplant.

optionExplanations.A: A two-year window allows the immune system to reconstitute sufficiently to handle the replication of a live attenuated vaccine virus safely.
optionExplanations.B: Six months is generally too early for HSCT patients to safely receive live vaccines due to the slow recovery of cellular immunity.
optionExplanations.C: While inactivated vaccines can often be started earlier, live vaccines require a more conservative wait time of two years.
optionExplanations.D: While long-term monitoring is required, most patients can begin their revaccination schedule with live vaccines after two years.

source.hint: This interval is exactly two years post-transplant.
